title: Knowledge check: v-if Versus v-show

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “v-if Versus v-show”?
options: v-if only changes the element color.
v-html is a safe visibility directive for user input.
Use v-if to create or remove conditional content; use v-show when repeated visibility toggles should use CSS display instead.
v-show removes its element from the DOM.
questions.answer_key: Use v-if to create or remove conditional content; use v-show when repeated visibility toggles should use CSS display instead.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses v-if Versus v-show directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Element creation and removal”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Custom directives are the best tool for all component reuse.
Use v-if to create/remove conditional content and v-show when toggling CSS visibility is more appropriate.
v-html is the safe default for user-generated HTML.
v-show always removes the element from the DOM.
questions.answer_key: Use v-if to create/remove conditional content and v-show when toggling CSS visibility is more appropriate.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Element creation and removal”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “v-if Versus v-show” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.
